newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to keep visa-free access from Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Canada to keep visa-free access from Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong passport holders will still be able to enter Canada without visitor visas after China takes the colony over from Britain on July 1, the Canadian government said on Wednesday.
"We are in the position to announce officially that there won't be a requirement of a visa for visitors from Hong Kong," Immigration Minister Lucienne Robillard told a news briefing.

Holders of the Hong Kong British National Overseas passport and, as of July 1, the Chinese Special Administrative Region passport, will not need visitor visas for Canada, the government said in a statement.
The announcement came after Canada received confirmation from China that it would support Canada's agreement with Hong Kong on dealing with illegal Hong Kong immigrants.
Robillard said Canada had problems removing unwanted Chinese from Canada and did not want the same problems with Hong Kong when it was returned to China.
"We were looking for the official support of the Chinese government and we have received that support," Robillard told a media briefing.
More than 200,000 people from Hong Kong travel to Canada each year. About half a million Canadians of Hong Kong descent live in Canada.
Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said Canada was the only country besides Britain that had made a commitment to continue visa-free access to people from Hong Kong.
Axworthy said he planned to visit Hong Kong and Beijing in about two weeks to discuss other issues linked to the transfer of Hong Kong to China from British rule.
He said Canada must still deal with the issue of people with dual passports, since China had told people from Hong Kong who hold two passports to choose between them, Axworthy said.
He said the government would launch a campaign next week for 150,000 people with Canadian and Hong Kong passports about how to make a choice and get proper documents.
